unit.why: A brief anecdote about Maimonides persuading a man who would not recite the great confession on Yom Kippur eve, followed by homiletic reasons for confessing even sins one did not commit; it is not about Hasidic figures.

stories.start_quote: מעשה שהיה בימי רבינו הגדול הרמב״ם
stories.summary_en: A man refused to say the great confession on Yom Kippur eve because he believed he had not committed those sins; Maimonides summoned him and explained that no one is free of sin, and the text then adds kabbalistic and moral reasons for everyone to confess every sin.

tags.why: Laudatory anecdote about Maimonides, a pre-Hasidic authority, cited from Siddur Nehora Shalem

quotes: ומה גם לפי הטעם שכתבו המקובלים ז״ל
עוד טעם אחר כתבו שכל ישראל ערבים זה לזה
tags.why: The short narrative is wrapped in an extended homiletic justification of the confession

quotes: שלא רצה לומר הוידוי הגדול בערב יוה״כ
tags.why: Set on the eve of Yom Kippur

quotes: צריך כל אדם להתוודות על כל חטא וחטא
tags.why: Recitation of the liturgical confession is the subject

quotes: ויתוודה בלב נשבר ונדכה ופלגי מים ירדו עיניו
tags.why: Confession as part of repentance is the theme

quotes: כי אמר שיודע שלא חטא כ״כ חטאים
tags.why: The man's self-righteous claim of sinlessness is implicitly rebuked

quotes: ע״כ צריך כל אדם להתוודות על כל חטא וחטא
tags.why: Maimonides rules on the obligation to recite the full confession

tags.why: A prior incarnation is offered as a reason for confession, but it is discussed, not depicted
